approved: Higher Education Support Amendment (Australia’s Economic Accelerator) Bill 2022
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would let the minister give grants for industry-led postgraduate research and for university research that moves technologies towards commercial readiness in priority sectors.
It sets up an Australia's Economic Accelerator Advisory Board of up to eight members to advise the minister on grants and a research commercialisation strategy updated every five years.
The board must produce an annual investment plan and a yearly report to parliament on program performance and barriers to commercialising university research.
Allow the minister to make grants under Part 2-3 of the Higher Education Support Act 2003 for industry-led postgraduate programs.
Create the Australia's Economic Accelerator Advisory Board to advise the minister and oversee priority managers.
Require a research commercialisation strategy every five years, with the first one due soon after the amendments start.
Mandate an annual investment plan from the board each financial year.
Require the board to give the minister an annual report for parliament.
Add new rules for handling program information.
Higher education providers, researchers, industry partners, and the Australia's Economic Accelerator Advisory Board and its priority managers.

The Higher Education Support Amendment (Australia's Economic Accelerator) Bill 2022 was referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration at the adjournment of the second reading debate.

The coalition supported the bill, which reintroduces their $2.2 billion University Research Commercialisation Package, including a $1.6 billion Australia’s Economic Accelerator program and six trailblazer university projects focused on national manufacturing priorities.

The speaker argued that the Higher Education Support Amendment (Australia's Economic Accelerator) Bill 2022 is needed to bridge the gap between Australia's world-class research (ranked 5th globally) and its poor commercialisation (ranked 37th), by establishing the Australia's Economic Accelerator program and a National Industry PhD Program to fund research translation and industry partnerships.
